Jordan / team —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a set of concrete asks so we can size and propose the right path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private). High-level notes from our discovery: 

- Primary drivers: PHI/PII handling in inference pipeline, predictable latency for triage flows (~150–200ms p50 target), and procurement preferring clear SLA/escape hatch.
- Current usage profile: short, chat-like requests with a median prompt length ~120 tokens and spikes at ~500 requests/min during morning triage windows.
- Compliance note: you mentioned SOC2 evidence and audit log retention (12 months).

Open asks (please confirm / fill in):
1) Isolation requirement: do you need physical tenancy (single-tenant GPUs) or is logical isolation within our Dedicated pool acceptable if we can meet latency + audit requirements?
2) SLOs: is 200ms p50 and 600ms p95 acceptable as a target, or do you need stricter guarantees?
3) Throughput: can you share a 7-day look at concurrent sessions / QPS and an expected growth multiplier for 6 months?
4) Data handling: any restrictions on in-flight caching (we support disabling prefix caching and audited KV cache controls) or must all request context be non-persistent?

I've attached the minimal requirements template you mentioned (ava_health_requirements.xlsx) — please populate if easier than inline replies.

Next steps I suggest:
- You answer the three bullets above;
- If you lean toward Dedicated/Private, we'll schedule a 45-minute tech deep-dive with Ben (SRE/SE) to walk through isolation architecture, fallback policies, and evidence we can provide;
- If Hosted API keeps looking viable, we'll propose a performance/observability addendum and a short PoC to validate p95 overheads.

I'll hold a tentative slot for the deep-dive on 04/15 if that works — open to shifting.

Best,

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the recap, that matches our notes. Quick answers inline below and attaching our security one-pager as requested.

1) Isolation: We have two product surfaces — an internal clinician triage tool (high sensitivity) and a patient-facing FAQ assistant (low sensitivity). For the clinician triage tool we strongly prefer a Dedicated pool with physical node separation if cost delta isn't prohibitive. For the public FAQ, Hosted API is fine.

2) SLOs: Clinician triage needs p50 <= 200ms and p95 <= 450ms. If you can provide a documented SLA for the dedicated tier that includes those numbers, that's ideal.

3) Throughput: Our engineering team says baseline 80 qps during weekdays, spikes to 420 qps for 10–15 minute windows. Growth estimate ~2x over 6 months.

4) Data handling: Clinician tool must not persist user prompts beyond request lifetime. We need logs/audit trails but no KV cache retention for sensitive prompts.

Next: Ben — can you confirm whether Redwood's Dedicated pool can be configured with strict no-persistence for KV/prefix caches and what fallback behavior would look like if that pool reaches capacity?

Attaching: security_one-pager.pdf

Thanks,

Sean / Marissa / Jordan —

Thanks for the details — here are concrete answers and a proposed path. I attached a quick sketch and a short CSV with SLA tiers.

1) Physical tenancy: Yes — Redwood Dedicated supports assigning a single-tenant GPU pool (customer-dedicated nodes). Lead time is typically 2–3 weeks for capacity allocation in our us-west region, shorter with reserved capacity. The pool is isolated at the hypervisor level; network and KMS integration are optional for Private deployments.

2) No-persistence for KV/prefix cache: We can disable prefix caching per-route and enforce zero-disk-cache policy for specific model endpoints. For additional assurance we can run those requests through an in-memory-only runtime (no checkpoint writes) and provide signed attestations for that configuration during onboarding.

3) Fallback behavior: Policy options —
- Strict: Fail-fast with 429 and notify client (recommended for highest-sensitivity workflows).
- Graceful: Route overflow to a Hosted variant with tokenization and redaction pre-processing (only for non-sensitive routes).
- Canary: Start with a 10% traffic mirror to Hosted to confirm compatibility, then increase.

Given your p95 target (<=450ms) and spikes to 420 qps, we recommend: Dedicated pool sized for peak with autoscale headroom (reserve 30% headroom), request queuing disabled for clinician routes (to avoid tail latency), and a fail-fast policy. That keeps p95 predictable.

4) Cost / procurement guidance: Rough delta vs Hosted API (ballpark monthly):
- Hosted (peak traffic, managed): $X — lower up-front, higher per-token costs, no node reservation;
- Dedicated (single-tenant node pool, reserved): ~2.4x Hosted for comparable traffic when reserving 4x the serving capacity for headroom. I'll give a tighter number if you share expected token volumes (I used a 120-token median).

Suggested onboarding steps (45–60 days):
- Procurement: sign reserved capacity LOI (2–3 weeks to provision nodes)
- Tech deep-dive (45m) — architecture, KMS, network;
- PoC week: run clinician traffic split 80/20 (Dedicated/Hosted mirror) to validate p95 and audit logging;
- SLA addendum: sign off (I attached sla-options.csv).

Attached: dedicated_config_sketch.png (png - architecture sketch), sla-options.csv (csv - SLA tiers & commitments)

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk the sketch.

—Ben
